title: $\eta$ is compatible with identities
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a condensed ring ([sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]) and $X$ a scheme. Then
$\eta_{\mathrm{id}_X}\colon\Lambda_X\to(\mathrm{id}_X)_*\Lambda_X$
([def-sfb-eta]) is the inverse of the canonical identity isomorphism
$i_X\colon(\mathrm{id}_X)_*\cong\mathrm{id}$ at $\Lambda_X$.
Here the pushforward is that of [def-sfb-finite-lower-star], and $i_X$ is induced
by the canonical projection $V\times_X X\cong V$ on every object $V$ of
$X_{\mathrm{proét}}$.

proof.text: Put $\pi=\pi_X\colon X\to\Spec\Z$, $F=p^*\Lambda$, $L=\pi^*$ and $R=\pi_*$. By [def-sfb-upper-star-from-point] and [def-sfb-alpha], $\Lambda_X=LF$. Write $A=(\mathrm{id}_X)^*$ and $B=(\mathrm{id}_X)_*$. By [def-sfb-alpha] and [def-sfb-pullback-from-point-comp-iso], $\alpha_{\mathrm{id}_X}$ is the component $d_F\colon ALF\to LF$ of the inverse pullback composition isomorphism, with $\pi\circ\mathrm{id}_X=\pi$ understood. If $v$ is the unit of $A\dashv B$, [def-sfb-eta] gives $\eta_{\mathrm{id}_X}=B(d_F)\circ v_{LF}$.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 1: identify the coefficient sheaf, alpha and eta

proof.text:
Let $u$ be the unit of $L\dashv R$, using [def-sfb-finite-upper-lower-star-adjunction], and let $c\colon RB\xrightarrow{\sim}R$ be the pushforward composition isomorphism of [def-sfb-finite-lower-star-comp], identifying $\pi\circ\mathrm{id}_X$ with $\pi$. By [def-sfb-finite-upper-star-comp], the inverse comparison component $d\colon AL\to L$ is the conjugate of $c^{-1}\colon R\to RB$; this is the inverse-direction form of the defining conjugation for the pullback comparison. The composite adjunction $AL\dashv RB$ has unit $R(v_{LF})\circ u_F$ by [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] with $L_1=AL$, $R_1=RB$, $L_2=L$, $R_2=R$, and $\delta=c^{-1}$. Its unit equation, followed by substitution from Step 1 and functoriality of $R$, is
$$
R(\eta_{\mathrm{id}_X})\circ u_F
=RB(d_F)\circ R(v_{LF})\circ u_F
=c^{-1}_{LF}\circ u_F.
$$

source.place: Proof, paragraph 2: the adjoint of eta, with the composite unit written out

proof.text:
For any sheaf $G$ on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ and $V$ on $(\Spec\Z)_{\mathrm{proét}}$, put $W=V\times_{\Spec\Z}X$. By [def-sfb-finite-lower-star] and [def-sfb-finite-lower-star-comp], both $c_G^{-1}$ and $R(i_{X,G}^{-1})$ on sections over $V$ are the restriction map
$$G(W)\longrightarrow G(W\times_X X)$$
along $q\colon W\times_X X\to W$, the first projection. Indeed the canonical pasting map $(V\times_{\Spec\Z}X)\times_X X\to V\times_{\Spec\Z}X$ has projections to $V$ and $X$ equal to $\operatorname{pr}_V\circ q$ and $\operatorname{pr}_X\circ q$: the latter equality is the defining fibre-product relation. These projections determine the map to $V\times_{\Spec\Z}X$, so it is $q$. Equality at every $V$ gives $c_G^{-1}=R(i_{X,G}^{-1})$.

source.place: Proof, paragraphs 3–4: establish the left unit law on sections by its two projections

proof.text:
Apply Step 3 with $G=LF=\Lambda_X$ to Step 2. We obtain
$$R(\eta_{\mathrm{id}_X})\circ u_F=R(i_{X,LF}^{-1})\circ u_F.$$
Under the Hom bijection of [def-sfb-finite-upper-lower-star-adjunction] for $\pi$, a morphism $h\colon LF\to BLF$ corresponds to $R(h)\circ u_F$. Since that correspondence is injective, the displayed equality proves $\eta_{\mathrm{id}_X}=i_{X,\Lambda_X}^{-1}$, as required.
